title: Finite subsets of a coalgebra lie in finite-dimensional subcoalgebras
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and $C$ a $k$-vector space with linear maps $\Delta:C\to C\otimes_k C$ and $\epsilon:C\to k$ satisfying coassociativity and both counit identities. Tensor products use [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. For every finite subset $S\subset C$ there is a finite-dimensional $k$-linear subspace $D\subset C$ containing $S$ such that $\Delta(D)\subset D\otimes_kD$, with the latter tensor product identified with its image in $C\otimes_kC$. The restrictions of $\Delta$ and $\epsilon$ make $D$ a coalgebra and its inclusion a coalgebra homomorphism. The empty subset and the zero coalgebra are allowed; neither cocommutativity nor finite-dimensionality of $C$ is assumed.

source.place: Proposition 4.7, printed p.86 (proof uses only comodule identities), and coefficient coalgebras in §9(d), printed pp.174–175; applied to the regular comodule, as in Theorem 12.18(c)⇒(d), printed p.238.

proof.text: Regard $C$ as a right $C$-comodule with coaction $\Delta$: its comodule equations are precisely coassociativity and the right counit identity in the hypotheses. Apply [lem-sfb-comodule-finite-subcomodule] to $M=C$ and $T=S$. Obtain a finite-dimensional subspace $V\subset C$ containing $S$, with the restricted coaction $\rho_V:V\to V\otimes_k C$.

source.place: Proposition 4.7, printed p.86, and §9(d), printed pp.174–175; the regular-comodule application is explicitly used in Theorem 12.18(c)⇒(d), printed p.238.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-finite-comodule-coefficient-coalgebra] to this finite-dimensional right $C$-comodule $V$. For a finite basis $(e_i)_{i\in I}$ of $V$, write $\Delta(e_j)=\sum_{i\in I}e_i\otimes c_{ij}$ in $C\otimes_k C$. That lemma gives the finite-dimensional coefficient coalgebra $D=\operatorname{span}_k\{c_{ij}:i,j\in I\}$, with the restrictions of $\Delta,\epsilon$ and with coalgebra inclusion into $C$.

source.place: Proposition 4.7, printed p.86, and §9(d), printed pp.174–175; the regular-comodule application is explicitly used in Theorem 12.18(c)⇒(d), printed p.238.

proof.text: Apply $\epsilon\otimes1_C$ to the displayed formula for $\Delta(e_j)$. The left counit identity gives $e_j=\sum_{i\in I}\epsilon(e_i)c_{ij}\in D$. Since the $e_j$ span $V$, it follows that $S\subset V\subset D$. This proves every requested assertion. If $V=0$, the basis and its matrix coefficients are empty and $D=0$; thus the argument also includes $S=\varnothing$ and $C=0$.
